prompt:
Create one exact 2×2 pixel-art horizontal gaze atlas from the supplied reference. Canvas aspect ratio must be 128:70, with four equal complete 64×35 upper-face crops and no gutters, borders, labels, or extra panel. Cell order: top-left LEFT OPEN; top-right RIGHT OPEN; bottom-left LEFT HALF; bottom-right RIGHT HALF.

Use the provided angry face and its exact same-mood selected source. Preserve its identity, established angry expression, revised connected brow shape, hair/fringe, forehead, nose bridge, eye spacing, skin texture, dark amber-brown iris hue, pupil size, pixel clusters, and subdued palette. Keep both brows locked in their current shape and position in every cell. Make no brow or face redesign.

Only gaze direction and the upper eyelid amount may change. In each OPEN pair, both irises and pupils must shift together roughly one native pixel toward the same canvas side: in LEFT, both pupils move toward the left edge; in RIGHT, both move toward the right edge. Keep natural source-like convergence and eye alignment. Both pupils must visibly track the same direction; never leave one centered while the other shifts, and do not make the pair cross-eyed. Keep each compact iris inside its own aperture, with the original dark pupil and tiny muted warm glint. Sclera stays shaded and subdued; no cream-white horizontal bands, enlarged eye openings, round/vector-like pupils, or bright glints.

The bottom pair must be the selected source HALF aperture, with the upper lids descending over the upper portion of each iris. Keep the current lower lid fixed at native row 28, keep cheek pixels from row 29 onward identical to the source, and preserve all exterior pixels exactly. Do not widen the eye hole or lift/lower the lower lid. Change only upper-lid pixels needed for the half phase. Maintain the angry brow lock through row 24 and put gaze detail inside the existing eye mask (bottom exclusive row 29). Keep the brow and eye area stable across left/right pairs.

The four cells must remain directly comparable crops of the same face. Render clean, native-resolution stepped pixel-art anatomy without painterly blur or smoothing.
